description: Figure 8, titled “Sr ratio ablation study,” is a line plot that illustrates the relationship between the recent sequence ratio (Sr) and two performance metrics: GPU memory usage of the KV cache (in GB) and perplexity. The x-axis represents the Sr ratio, ranging from 0% to 100% in increments of 10%, and is labeled “Sr ratio (%)”. The y-axis on the left, labeled “KV Mem. (GB)”, is linear and spans from 0 to 25 GB in increments of 5 GB. The y-axis on the right, labeled “Perplexity”, is also linear and ranges from 0 to 60 in increments of 10. The plot contains two lines: one solid blue line with circular markers representing “KV Mem. (GB)” and one dashed red line with square markers representing “Perplexity”. As the Sr ratio increases from 0% to 100%, the blue line shows a steady decline in KV memory usage, starting at approximately 24.2 GB at 0% Sr and decreasing to about 11.0 GB at 100% Sr. The red dashed line for perplexity initially decreases from about 55 at 0% Sr to a minimum of approximately 53.5 at 40–60% Sr, forming a shallow trough, and then rises slightly to around 54.5 at 100% Sr. The plot visually demonstrates that increasing the Sr ratio reduces memory usage but has a non-monotonic effect on perplexity, with an optimal range around 40–60% Sr for minimal perplexity.
